items.stem: What best distinguishes a Revit wall from a wall drawn in 2D CAD?

options.text: The Revit wall is a data-rich object that reports type, height and area and updates views automatically
options.rationale: Correct: Revit elements carry information and propagate changes, unlike CAD lines.

options.text: The Revit wall is simply two parallel lines
options.rationale: That describes a CAD representation, not a BIM object.

options.text: A Revit wall cannot be scheduled
options.rationale: Revit walls can be scheduled because they carry data.

options.text: CAD walls update plans and sections automatically
options.rationale: CAD lines do not propagate changes across views.

items.explanation: Correct: Revit elements carry information and propagate changes, unlike CAD lines.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: You change a parameter on a door and every door of that kind in the model updates. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: type parameters affect all instances of that type.

options.text: Instance parameters would have changed only the selected door
options.rationale: Correct: instance parameters are local to the one element.
An instance parameter would not have updated every door.

options.text: Type and instance parameters behave identically
options.rationale: They differ precisely in scope of effect.

items.explanation: Correct: type parameters affect all instances of that type.

items.stem: An element is present in a 3D view but missing from a floor plan. What should you check first?

options.text: The view range of the plan view
options.rationale: Correct: view range commonly hides elements above or below the cut plane.

options.text: Whether the element was deleted from the model
options.rationale: It appears in 3D, so it has not been deleted.
Units do not control element visibility in a view.

options.text: The title block on the sheet
options.rationale: Title blocks do not affect what shows in a plan view.

items.explanation: Correct: view range commonly hides elements above or below the cut plane.
